yarn-troppo.meaning: Every fact kept: "on May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "Mike Cortese, who looks after District 4", "signed on October 6, 2026". Asides react to the original rather than add facts: "Twenty thousand.", "Not a bad effort, that.", "Fifty years, near enough to the day... well, near enough to the year, anyway."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "a big wrap", "the whole box and dice", "puttin' down roots", "goin' shoulder to shoulder". "pulled its weight in Nashville growin' up" undersells "playing an important role", since pulling your weight means doing your fair share.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like a local telling the news: "So get this.", "VOA got its mitts on", "done a cracker of a job", "The bloke behind it all".
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-5 yarn through every paragraph, with no swearing (within vulgarity 2): "And here's the bit that gets ya".
yarn-troppo.tone: The respectful, celebratory note survives under the yarn ("done a cracker of a job hangin' on to its language"); the closing quip about the date edges the civic report toward banter.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads like it was told that way: "Heaps of 'em ended up puttin' down roots in Nashville, Tennessee, and the rest spread out".
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied throughout: "mob", "big wrap", "box and dice", "mitts", "touched down", "cracker", "shoulder to shoulder", "the bloke behind it all".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the proclamation story, all its points in order, retold.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point survives: "May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "Peshmerga forces, U.S. troops and their allies workin' shoulder to shoulder", "signed on October 6, 2026".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "a big wrap", "gives a shout-out", "tips its hat", "touched down". "pullin' its weight in Nashville's growth and development" undersells "an important role".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural and unforced: "the first mob of Kurdish families", "VOA got hold of", "Heaps of 'em ended up settlin' in Nashville".
yarn-dinkum.register: Retold throughout in plain Aussie, but closer to level 4: some lines stay near the source ("The proclamation was signed on October 6, 2026.").
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the respectful report tone under the slang: "The place has turned into a real hub for Kurdish culture and community life."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth throughout: "Accordin' to an official proclamation VOA got hold of, the first lot of Kurdish families touched down in the United States on May 1, 1976."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied ("big wrap", "shout-out", "tips its hat", "hub"), with "Accordin' to" opening two paragraphs.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Clearly the news item, shape and points intact.

unharnessed.meaning: All facts kept: "cultural, social and economic development", "May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "who represents District 4".
unharnessed.sense: Mostly apt ("gives a big rap", "gives a nod", "teaming up"), but "giving them their dues" garbles "give them their due", and "pulling their weight" undersells "an important role".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural where it is Aussie ("the first mob of Kurdish families", "VOA got hold of"); "giving them their dues" is off-idiom.
unharnessed.register: Lighter than the brief: much stays close to news prose ("Metropolitan Nashville Council member Mike Cortese, who represents District 4, led the official recognition of the anniversary").
unharnessed.tone: Respectful news tone kept: "The city's become a proper hub for Kurdish cultural and community life."
unharnessed.flow: Readable; the long first sentence piles on ("has gone and officially marked the 50th anniversary of the first mob of Kurdish families landing in the U.S., giving them their dues").
unharnessed.variety: Some range ("mob", "first lot", "big rap", "nod", "shoulder to shoulder", "teaming up") for the little slang there is.

dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept, but the military cooperation is softened to "have pitched in together in the fight against terrorism".
dinkum-3.sense: Some terms strain: "The Big Smoke's turned into a real hub" (the Big Smoke means a big city as seen from the bush, odd for Nashville here), "its lingo" for a heritage language, "workin' hand in glove" (often implies collusion), "pitched in together" for armed cooperation.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Mostly natural ("So get this.", "VOA got its mitts on", "puttin' down roots"), with "The Big Smoke" dropped in as a stock phrase.
dinkum-3.register: A full level-5 retelling, no swearing (within vulgarity 2): "it's given 'em a proper pat on the back for everythin' they've chipped in".
dinkum-3.tone: Mostly respectful; "hangin' on to its lingo" is a shade flippant for cultural preservation.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads well; "that first mob" repeats "first mob" from the paragraph before.
dinkum-3.variety: Varied ("pat on the back", "chipped in", "mitts", "big rap", "Big Smoke", "hand in glove"), with "mob" twice.
dinkum-3.essence: Recognisably the report, retold, with a few points bent.

engine.meaning: Essentially the original, every fact kept.
engine.sense: The two swaps strain a little: "fronted up in the United States" (front up is to show up somewhere, as for an appointment) and "The Big Smoke has become an important centre".
engine.authenticity: Little Aussie, and it is dropped in: "fronted up", "Accordin' to the document", "The Big Smoke" in otherwise formal news prose.
engine.register: Largely untranslated for a level-5 brief: "The proclamation highlights the Kurdish community's efforts to preserve its language, culture, and traditions over the past five decades".
engine.tone: Keeps the report's formal, respectful tone: "honouring their contributions to the city's cultural, social and economic development".
engine.flow: Reads as the original; the lone "Accordin'" and "The Big Smoke" jar against the formal prose.
engine.variety: Only three changes ("fronted up", "Accordin'", "The Big Smoke").
engine.essence: The report itself, unchanged in character.
